Shopping at Union Market in Park Slope in 2011, I overheard a distinct, refined voice say “I don’t think mushrooms would be a good idea.”

I turned and saw it was Patrick Stewart, shopping for groceries with his future wife. He could tell I overheard him and gave me a smile and a wink. 

RIP.

and probably sounded insane. But I will never forget that very strange moment where I got to talk to my hero, no matter how brief, in a weird hotel ballroom in downtown manhattan. He couldn't have been kinder or more generous. 

This will be a loss I feel deeply, for a very long time.

properties.text: I was privileged to see him play Prospero in The Tempest at the Public Theater in NYC in '95. His command of Shakespeare was unparalleled. British actors often have a way of rendering Shakespeare's language into common speech that American actors just can't match. Stewart was among the best.

I met him so many times in the early '90s at NYC cons, he was a pretty nice guy despite the fact I was never the biggest Star Trek fan. 

He also was funny if you caught him in the right mood at panels. :3

I saw Patrick Stewart as Scrooge in A Christmas Carol at the Winter Garden Theater in NYC as a kid. Didn't realize it at the time, but probably one of the coolest things I ever got to do. RIP to an absolute legend.

I was privileged to see Patrick Stewart on stage once. Macbeth at the Brooklyn Academy of Music. An amazing contemporary styled production with a minimalist set. I vividly remember one scene, a monologue by Stewart as Macbeth as he made and ate a sandwich. He made it look so natural and real.
